title: White Label SEO for Small Web Design Studios
excerpt: How white label SEO, local SEO and GEO work for a small web design studio: what gets delivered, what your client sees, and how the first month runs.
content:
White label SEO means a specialist team does the SEO work for your clients while you sell it, report it and keep the relationship under your own brand. For a small web design studio it is the fastest way to offer SEO, local SEO and AI visibility (GEO) without hiring. Your client sees one partner: you.

This guide explains how the setup works in practice, what gets delivered, what your client sees, and what the first month looks like.

What is white label SEO and how does it work for a small studio?

Your studio builds great websites. Then the client asks, "How do we get found on Google?" If you do not sell SEO, that question usually ends with the client hiring another agency, and sometimes that agency rebuilds the site too.

With white label SEO you say yes instead. The model is simple:

  • You sell the SEO service at your own price, under your own brand.
  • Your white label partner does the research, the fixes, the content and the tracking.
  • Reports go out with your logo and your name on them.
  • You stay the only contact for the client.

You pay the partner a wholesale fee and keep the margin. More important for most studios, you keep the client, because the website, the search work and the monthly conversation all stay with you.

What is delivered, and what does the end client see?

A good white label partnership covers the full search picture, not only keywords. At asparagents a partner studio can offer:

  • On-page and technical SEO: titles, meta descriptions, headings, internal links, structured data, speed and indexing checks.
  • Local SEO: Google Business Profile setup and management, categories, services, photos, review strategy and consistent name, address and phone details across the web.
  • GEO / AI visibility: making the client's business clear and easy to cite for AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews.
  • Content: service pages and articles written for real search questions.
  • Monthly reporting: a plain-language report on rankings, traffic, profile activity and AI mentions, ready to send under your brand.

The end client sees your reports, your emails and your invoices. They do not see our name unless you choose to tell them. We do not contact your clients directly unless you ask us to join a call, and then we join as part of your team.

Why do clients now ask about AI visibility, and how does GEO sit next to SEO?

Business owners are starting to ask AI assistants for recommendations: "Who is a good dentist near me?" or "Which accountant in Leeds works with small companies?" The answer often names a few businesses and links to a few sources. If your client is not one of them, they lose that customer before any search result is clicked.

GEO, short for Generative Engine Optimization, is the work that makes a business easy for these systems to understand and recommend. It does not replace SEO. It builds on it:

  • The same clear service pages that rank in Google also give AI assistants facts to quote.
  • A complete Google Business Profile feeds both the map results and many AI answers about local businesses.
  • Consistent details on the website, the profile and directories help both search engines and AI models trust that the business is real.

For a studio this is a strong reason to add search services now. You built the site, so you are the natural person to make it visible in both places.

How can a studio add SEO, local SEO and GEO without hiring?

Hiring an SEO specialist only makes sense once you have enough SEO clients to keep that person busy. Until then, white label lets you grow the service first and decide on hiring later. A practical way to start:

  • Pick your offer. Start with one package, for example a local SEO and GEO plan for clients who already have a site you built.
  • Set your price. Price it for your market and your margin. Your partner's fee is your cost, not your client's price.
  • Start with your current clients. Clients who trust your work are the easiest first sales. A short audit of their site is often enough to start the conversation.
  • Agree on communication. Decide who writes to the client, how fast questions are answered and where tasks are tracked.
  • Review the first reports together. Make sure the format and tone sound like your studio before they go out.

What do onboarding and the first month look like?

A clear first month is what makes a client stay. With asparagents it usually runs like this:

  • Kickoff: a short call with you to agree on goals, target areas and the services each client gets.
  • Access: website, Google Search Console, Google Analytics and Google Business Profile access, shared by you or your client.
  • Week 1: an audit of the site, the profile and how the business shows up in search and in AI answers today.
  • Weeks 2 to 4: the quick wins first, such as technical fixes, page titles, profile gaps and inconsistent business details, then the content plan.
  • End of month 1: the first white label report, with what was done, what changed and what comes next.

Local search results move with relevance, distance and prominence, so early wins usually come from fixing relevance: the right categories, services and page content. Prominence, such as reviews and mentions, builds over the following months.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will my client know I use a white label partner?

Only if you tell them. Reports, emails and deliverables carry your brand. You can simply introduce us as your SEO team.

Do I need SEO knowledge to sell white label SEO?

You need enough to explain the value and answer basic questions. Your partner handles the technical work and can join client calls as part of your team when a question goes deeper.

Can I offer only local SEO or only GEO?

Yes. You can start with one service and add others later. Local SEO is often the easiest start, because most clients of a small studio serve one city or region.

Who owns the client and the accounts?

You do. The client relationship, the contract and the access stay with your studio or your client.
